column1: # Copyright holders for the standard license texts rust_crates.py generates
# (<crate>-<version>/LICENSE-<id>.generated.txt), for a crate that ships no
# text of a license it is used under AND whose Cargo `authors` are not (all)
# Columns, tab-separated: crate, license (the SPDX id of the generated text,
# or * for any), holders (what follows "Copyright (c) " in the text; " | "
# between holders gives each its own copyright line), evidence (the file on
# disk that names them, as a path in the local Cargo registry,
# ~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/, with the words that show it).
# A row for a crate that is no longer linked, or that now ships the text
# itself, is reported as unused and can go.

column4: alloc-no-stdlib-2.0.4/LICENSE: "Copyright (c) 2016 Dropbox, Inc." — alloc-stdlib ships no license file and is published from the same repository (Cargo.toml: repository = "https://github.com/dropbox/rust-alloc-no-stdlib"), whose LICENSE this is

brotli-decompressor-5.0.0/LICENSE: "Copyright (c) 2016 Dropbox, Inc." — brotli ships only the Brotli Authors' MIT text (LICENSE.MIT); its BSD-3-Clause half is Dropbox's code, whose license brotli-decompressor (same authors, github.com/dropbox) carries
objc-0.2.7/LICENSE.txt: "Copyright (c) Steven Sheldon" — objc2-0.6.4/CHANGELOG.md: "Forked the project, so the crate name is now `objc2`" (a fork of objc)
block-0.1.6/Cargo.toml: authors = ["Steven Sheldon"], license = "MIT" — block2-0.6.2/CHANGELOG.md: "Forked the project, so it is now available under the name `block2`" (a fork of block)

objc-0.2.7/LICENSE.txt: "Copyright (c) Steven Sheldon" — objc2-encode-4.1.0/CHANGELOG.md: "Forked the project, so it is now available under the name `objc2-encode`" (a fork of Steven Sheldon's objc-encode, whose 0.0.1–1.1.0 releases it lists)
